# Reg M-C meta analysis — usage, sets, archetypes, bring/lead, Bo3 adaptation

Date: 2026-09-23. Historical findings record under `docs/_reports/`; not a living document and not current state.
**Generated by `node solver/meta/report.js`** from `solver/out/meta/*.json`; every figure is read from those artifacts.
Store read at 2026-09-23T07:37:09.843Z (manifest `solver/out/meta/manifest.json`). Open team sheets only. No win predictor from sheets.

## 0. Verdict

1. **Population:** 28,274 clean open-sheet games (27,715 bo3, 559 bo1), 6,822 players, 2026-09-09 08:08 → 2026-09-23 06:38 UTC. 39,096 of 67,370 store games excluded, 37,486 of them closed-sheet bo1. Legality was read from the M-C checkout (`pokemon-showdown-mc` @ `f10d6798f2`, equal to the pin); every kept game passes it.
2. **Usage moves fast and the intervals are wide.** Games cluster heavily by player (design effect on species shares ~19×), so a Wilson interval on game counts understates the uncertainty by ~4.4×. Even so, first week vs last week flags 12 species risers and 17 fallers at BH q<0.05.
3. **Archetypes: no k met the pre-set stability bar** (median bootstrap ARI ≥ 0.80). The fallback took the most stable k, **k=8** (median ARI 0.7696); 6 of 8 clusters are individually stable (Jaccard ≥ 0.75). Archetype win rates sit within a few points of 50%; after the Elo correction and BH, 1 of 8 archetypes differ from their pilots' expectation.
4. **Bo3 adaptation is large and result-driven:** the same four is brought again 61.0% of the time after a win and 29.7% after a loss (win minus loss +31.3 pp, cluster 95% +29.9 pp to +32.7 pp). Sheets never change within a series (0 of 20,984).
5. **Stat Points are not in the store** (evs null on every slot), so the set library has no spreads.

Paths: code `solver/meta/`, test `solver/tests/test-meta-lib.js`, artifacts `solver/out/meta/` (`manifest.json`, `games.clean.jsonl.gz`, `usage.json`, `sets.json`, `archetypes.json`, `bringlead.json`, `bo3.json`).

## 2. Usage over time

**Unit:** share of side-games (one player's sheet in one game) whose sheet contains the entity; 56,548 side-games. Moves, items and abilities are "share of teams carrying it", not per-slot. **Player share** = share of the 6,822 players who showed it at least once.
**Intervals:** Wilson on side-game counts (as asked), and beside it a cluster-robust interval by player (linearised ratio estimator). The cluster interval is the honest one; the design effect column is the variance ratio between them.
**Weeks:** W0 = 2026-09-09…2026-09-15 (27,180 sides); W1 = 2026-09-16…2026-09-22 (28,496 sides); W2 = 2026-09-23…2026-09-23 (872 sides). The last week is partial.
**Rating bands:** tertiles of rated side-games — low < 1080 ≤ mid < 1150 ≤ high; unrated separate; top decile ≥ 1250. Sides: low 16,579, mid 15,950, high 16,687, unrated 7,332, top decile 4,775. The bo3 and bo1 ladders are separate Elo pools; bo1 is 2.0% of games.
**Risers/fallers:** period A = 2026-09-09…2026-09-15, period B = 2026-09-17…2026-09-23; pB - pA, cluster-robust SE by player (joint linearisation, so a player in both periods is handled), two-sided z, BH-FDR over every entity of the category with >= 30 side-games in A+B; flagged when q < 0.05.

NOT AVAILABLE — the store records no Stat Points (evs null on every slot); a set here has no spread. ## 4. Archetypes

**Method.** spherical k-means on the binary species-of-six vector; one point per distinct (player, six); k-means++ init; best of 8 restarts for the reference fit. 13,632 points over 280 species. Every side-game is then assigned to the nearest centroid of the reference fit.
**Choosing k.** k* = the largest k in the grid whose median bootstrap ARI >= 0.80 (B=20 resamples of distinct player-teams, each refit and re-assigned to all teams, compared with the full-data fit). Hennig 2007 cluster-wise Jaccard: >= 0.75 stable, 0.6-0.75 doubtful, < 0.6 dissolves.

| k | median ARI | p10 ARI | min ARI | clusters Jaccard ≥ 0.75 | clusters < 0.6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.4508 | 0.3294 | 0.2268 | 0/3 | 1 |
| 4 | 0.4708 | 0.3534 | 0.2978 | 1/4 | 2 |
| 5 | 0.5955 | 0.3979 | 0.3881 | 2/5 | 2 |
| 6 | 0.695 | 0.5337 | 0.4313 | 3/6 | 2 |
| **8** | 0.7696 | 0.554 | 0.4759 | 6/8 | 0 |
| 10 | 0.6617 | 0.527 | 0.3959 | 4/10 | 2 |
| 12 | 0.6739 | 0.5815 | 0.5569 | 6/12 | 3 |
| 14 | 0.6653 | 0.5603 | 0.5437 | 5/14 | 4 |
| 16 | 0.597 | 0.5371 | 0.5288 | 2/16 | 6 |
| 20 | 0.533 | 0.4153 | 0.3869 | 1/20 | 16 |
| 24 | 0.5241 | 0.4795 | 0.4613 | 2/24 | 18 |

**No k reached median ARI 0.80, so the pre-set rule was not met.** The fallback — the k with the highest median ARI — is **k = 8** (0.7696). That is a real peak (it beats both neighbours on median and on stable-cluster count), but it is "moderately stable", not "stable": 6 of 8 clusters clear Jaccard 0.75 and the rest are doubtful. Team space is a continuum with dense cores, and k-means cuts the continuum differently on every resample.

**Labels are derived**: the species present on ≥ 50% of the cluster's side-games, most frequent first (up to three). Win rate uses decided games (winner known, an action taken, ≥ 3 turns) and excludes mirrors. The Elo residual is observed win minus the Elo expectation from both players' ladder ratings — it asks whether the archetype wins more than its pilots' ratings predict. It is a confound correction, not a predictor. q = BH over archetypes.

## 5. Bring and lead behaviour

**Censoring.** Only revealed Pokémon are known to have been brought. 45,452 of 56,548 sides revealed all four ("full bring"); leads are known on 56,026. The bring rate is computed on full-bring sides and the revealed-only lower bound over all sides is printed beside it. full-bring sides are games long enough to reveal four; a species kept in the back and never sent in is under-counted by the revealed lower bound, and the full-bring subset over-represents long games.

## 6. Bo3 adaptation

**Series linkage** comes from the raw log (`raw log `|uhtml|bestof|` link (game-bestof3-<id>); game number from the same line`), not from guessing. 13,036 series; games of each present in the clean store: 1 game: 2,544, 2 games: 6,305, 3 games: 4,187. 20,984 player-series have ≥ 2 games; the six changed within a series in **0** of them. 29,320 game-to-game transitions (player's view). Intervals are cluster-robust by player.

| transition | n | rate | Wilson | cluster 95% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| same four, any | 20,088 | 43.4% | 42.7%–44.1% | 42.4%–44.4% |
| same four, after a WIN | 8,820 | 61.0% | 60.0%–62.0% | 59.7%–62.3% |
| same four, after a LOSS | 11,268 | 29.7% | 28.8%–30.5% | 28.5%–30.8% |
| same lead pair, any | 28,988 | 34.7% | 34.2%–35.3% | 33.8%–35.6% |
| same lead pair, after a WIN | 14,494 | 47.1% | 46.3%–47.9% | 45.9%–48.3% |
| same lead pair, after a LOSS | 14,494 | 22.3% | 21.6%–23.0% | 21.4%–23.2% |
| same four, game 1 → 2 | 13,880 | 41.7% | 40.9%–42.6% | 40.6%–42.9% |
| same four, game 2 → 3 | 6,208 | 47.1% | 45.9%–48.4% | 45.7%–48.5% |
| same lead, game 1 → 2 | 20,448 | 34.1% | 33.4%–34.7% | 33.1%–35.1% |
| same lead, game 2 → 3 | 8,540 | 36.2% | 35.2%–37.2% | 35.0%–37.4% |
| BASELINE same four: game 1 of next series, same six | 7,505 | 20.5% | 19.6%–21.4% | 19.3%–21.8% |
| BASELINE same lead: game 1 of next series, same six | 12,081 | 20.2% | 19.5%–20.9% | 19.3%–21.1% |

Loss minus win: same four -31.3 pp (cluster 95% -32.7 pp to -29.9 pp); same lead pair -24.8 pp (-26.0 pp to -23.6 pp). Of the four brought, the number kept into the next game: after a win {"2":765,"3":2677,"4":5378} (mean 3.523); after a loss {"2":2497,"3":5429,"4":3342} (mean 3.075). At least two of the four are always kept — that is forced (six on the sheet, four brought), not a behaviour.

**The baseline is the important row.** Against a NEW opponent the same player with the same six repeats the same four only 20.5% of the time. So the bring is opponent-conditioned before any adaptation happens, and within a series — same opponent — even the losers repeat more than the cross-opponent habit (29.7% vs 20.5%). "Win-stay, lose-shift" is the shape; the size is the win/loss gap, not the gap to the baseline.

Species-level adaptation is small: players swap one or two slots, and the swaps are spread across many species, so no single species moves much in aggregate. Whether a swap ANSWERS the opponent's previous bring needs a counter model and was not attempted.

## 7. Limits — what this does not say

- **Two weeks of data.** "Riser" means period B differs from period A; it is not a trend estimate. The state-space smoother the research note suggests needs more periods than two full weeks.
- **Cluster-robust ≠ fully independent.** Players are clusters; a bo3 series is nested inside a player. Two players in one game share a game-level shock that the player clustering does not absorb for two-sided quantities.
- **Win rate by archetype is observational.** The Elo residual corrects for pilot rating only.
- **Bring rates are censored** (§5). A Pokémon that sat in the back all game is invisible in the lower bound and its side is dropped from the full-bring rate.
- **Archetypes are moderately stable, not stable.** Treat the doubtful clusters as neighbourhoods, not types. Species usage and sets do not depend on the clustering.
- **bo1 is almost absent** after the custom-room exclusion; every table is effectively the bo3 ladder.
- **No spreads.** Not in the store.

## 8. Reproduce

```
cmd.exe /c tools\lownode.cmd solver/meta/extract.js     # reads data/ + the M-C checkout, writes solver/out/meta/manifest.json + games.clean.jsonl.gz
cmd.exe /c tools\lownode.cmd solver/meta/analyze.js     # verifies the extract digest, writes the five analysis JSONs
node solver/meta/report.js                              # writes this file
node solver/tests/test-meta-lib.js                       # statistics, parsing, legality helpers
```

A re-run an hour later reads a larger store and is a different sample; compare manifests, not memory. Nothing under `engine/`, `tests/`, `web/` or `data/` was written, and no git command was run against this repository.
